thread:
pd-bot: SEV1 pager: serving runtime error rate above threshold in us-west-1 (cluster=usw1-prod). Auto-escalation to oncall-eng.
emma: seeing a huge uptick in ib retransmits on ib0 across rack-7. Packet drops + partial link down events reported.
raj: multiple pods on node-42 and node-45 restarting. Logs show repeated CUDA allocation failures during tokenizer init.
kelsey: can you paste the error from one of the pods? need a quick signal to customers.
raj: here from pod serve-6b2a:
```
E 07:02:11 runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
W 07:02:11 serving: aborting request, status=500
meminfo: total=128Gi free=3Gi rss=125Gi kv_cache_entries=17842
```
netops: switch event: TOR-7 port 3 (10.2.44.5) flapped at 07:01:47, moved to errdisable briefly. Physical layer showing increased CRC errors.
emma: we think retransmits caused request amplification -> kv cache warmed up repeatedly -> OOM cascade on GPUs.
infra-bot: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) reduce kv cache size 3) enable model fallback 4) throttle ingress retries
emma: executing cordon+drain on node-42 and node-45 now.
emma: `kubectl cordon node-42 && kubectl drain node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
raj: starting a fast configmap rollout to limit kv cache and enable short TTLs.
raj: config patch applied:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES: "1073741824"
  KV_CACHE_TTL_SECS: "60"
  DEDUPE_PER_REQUEST: "true"
  INGRESS_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS: "200"
```
kelsey: deploying a traffic split: 15% -> gpt-fallback-small in usw1 to reduce pressure on primary runtime.
deploy-bot: traffic-split applied for service/text-gen-usw1: 85% primary / 15% fallback
cs-ops: reporting customer impact: ~9 orgs experienced elevated 5xx rates; majority transient but one high-volume tenant saw 15% errors for ~10m.
emma: paused cluster autoscaler for usw1-prod to avoid bringing up new nodes while network is noisy.
netops: opened urgent ticket with colo network team; they are swapping patch and validating fiber to TOR-7.
raj: after cordon+config changes, OOMs dropped sharply; a handful of restarts persisted on node-45 which shares the same TOR.
kelsey: I'll take incident lead for the next shift. immediate action items: 1) confirm TOR stability 2) keep fallback in place 3) gather kernel dumps & GPU profiles 4) prepare customer note
emma: saving logs and artifacts to /incidents/2412345678/artifacts/ (includes pod logs, nvml traces, switch counters, kvmem profiles)
infra-bot: runbook referenced: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/serving-network-amplification
kelsey: post-incident owners: kelsey (RCA), netops (network RCA), raj (runtime mitigation). Targeting sev1 writeup in 6 hours with timeline and action items.
cs-ops: drafting customer comms now, will send once we validate the final remediation steps.
emma: TOR reported stable at 07:10:22, retransmits back at baseline, OOMs almost zero with current mitigating config.
raj: rolling restart of serving fleet scheduled at +30m to pick up safe defaults permanently; will keep canary traffic to fallback 10% for another hour.
kelsey: handing off active incident to oncall-kelsey. If re-pager occurs, escalate to infra lead @netops. Closing pager now but leaving channel open for follow-ups.
kelsey: summary note for postmortem: consider global ingress retry throttles per-TOR, limit kv cache growth on warmup, and autoscaler rules to not scale during partial networking failures. Will add recommended infra changes to RCA.
